commands.summary: Confirmed the implementation still matches the governing decisions after all concurrent merges. Decision 0056 stages Git explicitly: Stage 1 (this item) is SAF/archive import-export with no embedded Git dependency; Stage 2 is a future GitBackend abstraction distinct from the existing shell-shaped GitRunner trait, to be created or activated at this item's own closeout. Decision 0057 already reserves the seam in the registry model (acquisition_kind = remote_git, git_state = embedded_git_managed, both '[reserved, Stage 2]') and specifies the typed capability/status descriptor rather than callable clone/pull/push stubs. WI061's own AC-5 required that work/proposed/065 exist at WI061 closeout with no implementation -- confirmed true historically and structurally unchanged.

AC-9 half A (executable seam) verified structurally true, not merely documented: AcquisitionKind::{SafDirectory, SafArchive, RemoteGit} and GitState::{NonGit, GitMetadataPresent, EmbeddedGitManaged} already exist as reserved enum variants in registry.rs (RemoteGit/EmbeddedGitManaged are declared but never constructed by any Stage-1 code path); mobile-types.ts mirrors both enums exactly for the frontend. mobile_git_capabilities (mobile_acquisition.rs) returns a typed MobileCapabilityStatus with Stage2Status::UnsupportedStage2 for clone/pull/push -- a real typed capability descriptor, not a silent absence or a faked success. GitRunner (repopact-repository/src/git.rs) remains exactly the pre-existing shell-command-shaped trait (run(root, args, label) -> GitOutput); grepping the full rust/ tree found zero occurrences of a GitBackend trait -- it exists only as a specified requirement in decisions 0056/0057 and WI061's README, correctly left undefined until the Stage-2 item designs it. DesktopService, RepositorySession, RepositoryTopology's core repository model, and the MutationRequest -> MutationPlan -> MutationResult pipeline received zero changes across all of WI065 (confirmed by Checkpoint C's zero-diff proof and re-confirmed by grep/diff against origin/main); only the acquisition adapter is new. This satisfies AC-9 half A: the seam accommodates clone/pull/push and remote_git/embedded_git_managed without a breaking redesign, without forcing GitRunner to become something it is not.

Populated work-item.json with owner_scope=tooling, affected_scopes=[tooling, docs, evidence] (governance/owners.json only recognizes governance|work|evidence|tooling|docs as scope ids; mobile/desktop are not registered scopes), depends_on=["065"], a preflight note explaining the AC-9 provenance and the provider-neutral distinction from WI067, and 8 acceptance criteria (GIT-001..GIT-008) covering: a GitBackend abstraction distinct from GitRunner with Android git2-rs/libgit2 build-gating and a later gix re-evaluation; zero required changes to DesktopService/RepositorySession/RepositoryTopology/mutation pipeline/ROG authority/workspace identity; remote repositories remaining ordinary app-private working trees and never an alternate Repository authority; real clone/fetch/pull/push with protected credential storage and HTTPS-first; offline usability of previously cloned workspaces with explicit dirty/divergence/conflict handling and no silent destructive reset; a typed-only command/network surface (no generic HTTP proxy, no arbitrary URL fetcher, no shell); real Android (and shared-desktop) runtime proof; and security evidence (credential redaction, TLS failure behavior, auth expiry, cancellation, partial-clone cleanup). Failed twice first (work.unknown-owner-scope / work.unknown-affected-scope for 'mobile'/'desktop', which are not registered scope ids in governance/owners.json), corrected to owner_scope=tooling / affected_scopes=[tooling, docs, evidence] matching WI065's and WI067's own convention (their implementation also lives under rust/**, which the tooling scope owns), then passed clean: 'Repository governance validation passed.'
